title: Nuevo Laredo sets property tax record, topping 200 million pesos as city pays off inherited debt
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's property tax collections topped 200 million pesos for the first time, up 18% from the same period last year, as the city also paid off 580 million pesos of inherited public debt. November brings full forgiveness of surcharges for residents who catch up on what they owe.
content:
Nuevo Laredo's property tax collections have surpassed 200 million pesos for the first time in the city's history, growing 18% over the same period last year, according to Reynosa Press.

About 90,000 of the roughly 199,000 registered properties in the city have paid the tax so far, according to municipal records cited in the report. The city also announced it has fully paid off 580 million pesos of inherited public debt, leaving Nuevo Laredo debt-free and with more room to fund city projects, the report said.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal credited residents for responding to the city's payment options and investment in infrastructure, saying that when people see their contributions turned into public works and better services, they participate, according to Reynosa Press.

Tax incentives during 2026 have saved families more than 70 million pesos in surcharges, fees and enforcement costs tied to the property tax, the report said. During November, the city is forgiving 100% of surcharges, fees and collection costs on the property tax so residents with back balances can get current, and it is also forgiving 100% of surcharges on the property transfer tax, known as ISAI.

The city is also running a parking-meter regularization program offering 50% off fines and 100% off surcharges on violations accumulated since fiscal year 2022. About 65,000 pending fines worth around 18 million pesos are on the books, according to the report. Parking fines can be paid at OXXO stores as well as municipal cashier modules.

Residents with questions can visit the Ingresos offices on the ground floor of the El Palomar building, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., according to the report.

Sources: Reynosa Press, Nov. 11, 2026; La Voz Tamaulipas, Nov. 11, 2026.
